en.title: Two-Digit Cipher from Last Digits of Adjacent Sums
en.description:
Repeatedly form the next row from the last digits of the sums of adjacent digits until only 2 digits remain, then output them as a two-character string, keeping leading 0s.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n; the second line contains n digits. 2≤n≤5000, each in 0..9.
en.output: Output exactly two digit characters; leading 0s must be kept.
en.explanation: The answers are 04, 04 and 88; the third example has only one round, and the last digit of 9+9 is 8 in both positions.
hints: Update the adjacent sums modulo 10 in place from the front, shrinking the effective length by one each round until it reaches 2.
